title: Brazil–Chile Joint Declaration (August 2024) — Diplomatic Agreement Breach by ANAC Through Jurisdictional Avoidance
category: Breach of International Commitment / Violation of Treaty Obligations

confidence.note: The Joint Declaration was signed by Presidents Lula and Boric in August 2024, one month after the SCL incident, and explicitly encompasses human rights, consular cooperation, and access to justice. ANAC’s subsequent dismissal of the passenger’s complaint contradicts these commitments. Case update rates this as HIGH strength, cross‑reference BR‑013.

incident_timestamp_display: 5 August 2024 (Joint Declaration signed) – 3 December 2025 (ANAC dismissal). The breach crystallized upon ANAC’s dismissal of the complaint.
allegation_summary: On 5–6 August 2024, Brazilian President Lula and Chilean President Boric signed a Joint Presidential Declaration containing 58 bilateral agreement points, including commitments to human rights protection, consular cooperation, and citizen access to justice. This declaration, one month after the LA8159 incident, constitutes a binding international instrument that obliges all Brazilian state organs — including ANAC — to respect and protect the rights of affected individuals. Yet, on 3 December 2025, ANAC dismissed passenger Leandro Disconzi’s complaint (NUP 50001.115849/2025‑10) by claiming lack of jurisdiction over an incident that occurred in Chile. This dismissal directly contradicts the bilateral commitments to cooperation and access to justice, and violates the constitutional principle that international relations are governed by, among others, the prevalence of human rights (CF/88 Art. 4, II) and the duty to fulfill treaty obligations in good faith (VCLT Art. 26). ANAC’s act is a breach of an international obligation, undermining the diplomatic undertakings made by Brazil.
